matches.rationale: Pred1 identifies the Section 2.1 Theorem 2.2 reduction/proof as invalid and the NP-hardness claim as open, which directly captures GT1's corrupted interval-encoding reduction and unsound hardness proof.

Pred2 flags the Section 2.2 PTAS as not sound for arbitrary interval-overlap patterns, noting that the paper itself admits the general case requires further innovations. This matches GT2's claim that the PTAS's approximation guarantee is unjustified for general interval overlaps.
No finding addresses the fixed 8-chain interval structure or the experimental-design limitations described in GT3.
No finding addresses the implausible disagreement-rate improvements or unusually low standard deviations in Table 1.
No finding discusses overstatement of recovered intervals as reflecting political leanings or coalition membership.
No finding addresses the omission of ethical or privacy considerations for sensitive political voting data.
No finding addresses fabricated or unverifiable citations in the Related Work section.
No finding addresses the promotional abstract language claiming the method resolves drawbacks and recovers political leaning accurately.
No finding addresses the Conclusion's conjectures and future-work claims being disconnected from unresolved theoretical gaps.
No finding addresses the overstated runtime scalability or missing hardware and benchmark details in the experiments.
No finding addresses inconsistent definitions or notation for interval graphs and agreement functions across sections.
No finding addresses the absence of ethical oversight or privacy disclosure in the Conclusion.
No finding addresses abstract-level overclaiming of strong hardness results and a PTAS as complete or definitive.
No finding addresses the implausible result of algorithms outperforming ground truth under sign noise, producing negative normalized disagreement differences.
No finding addresses the missing initialization or ablation experiments for the GAIA and VENUS heuristics.
No finding addresses the causal language in the Introduction overstating that opinion intervals explain conflicts and user interactions.
